matching.formula: score = rank_score + sum over score keys k of (w_k x scores[k]) + CONFIRMED_BONUS when any apartment's checked.status is confirmed_today or price_changed_today
matching.weights: w_k starts at 0. For every answered single question, add the chosen answer's weights. Then, for each of the (at most two) answers picked in the pick_two question, in the order picked, for each key k in its weights: w_k = max(w_k, pick_floor) x that weight (2: doubled), so a key that matters most counts at least 2 x pick_floor. A skipped question adds nothing.
matching.must_haves: For every answered question whose chosen answer has a filter (only must_have questions have one) {field, op, value}: a building passes when fit[field] op value holds (op is <=, >= or ==). A null fit field passes. A building that fails any goes to 'Doesn't fit what you said', with the failed answer ids as reasons (its fit_misses text for each); nothing is deleted.
matching.order: Fitting buildings by score, highest first; equal scores by id, ascending. The non-fitting group is in the same order.

algorithm.version: 4: the choices are meta.recommender.conjoint tasks (eight, adaptive); next_pair, stop, sample_sets and sample_bests below are version 3's and no longer drive the page
algorithm.utility: U_w(b) = sum_k w_k x features[k] over `features` (sure excluded)
algorithm.group_score: each building's score is rounded to round_decimals; a group scores the expected mean of the two best of a random 3-building subset of its buildings (exact: (3 x mean - E[min of 3]) / 2, with P(the i-th best is the min) = C(i-1, 2) / C(n, 3), i counted from 1 in score order, best first); a group with fewer than three buildings is filled to three with the median building score of the whole set under the same weights (the mean of the two middle values when the count is even), then the mean of its two best. Why (coordinator, 2026-11-17): with the mean of its two best, a deep neighborhood wins by having many buildings to pick from (Newark, 20 buildings, was in the three for 197 of 200 simulated users); a one-building neighborhood is not treated as a deep one either
algorithm.likelihood: gap = U_w(a) - U_w(b); P(a) = sig((gap - either_band)/temperature); P(b) = sig((-gap - either_band)/temperature); P(either) = max(0, 1 - P(a) - P(b))
algorithm.posterior: pi_s = prod over answers (in order) of the likelihood, divided by the sum over samples; uniform if the sum is 0
algorithm.mean_weights: wbar_k = sum_s pi_s x w_s,k; expected utility = U_wbar
algorithm.eligible: order groups by round(score) desc, id; eligible = the first, plus any with rank < ceil(n x relevance_top_share) and round(score) >= round(relevance_floor x the first's score); if fewer than 3 are eligible, the recommendation is the eligible ones then the next by score (no diversity)
algorithm.mmr: among the eligible groups only (iterated in id order): s' = (score - min)/(max - min) over all groups (all 0 if max - min <= 1e-12); pick 3 greedily by round(lambda x s' - (1 - lambda) x max similarity to the picked, round_decimals), ties to the smaller id; similarity is group_similarity (1 - centroid distance / largest centroid distance, standardised features)
algorithm.sample_sets: for each sample, the MMR top three with that sample's weights, as sorted ids joined by '|'; computed once
algorithm.next_pair: pool = top pair_pool buildings by round(score_wbar) desc, id; pairs (a, b) with a < b by id, skipping pairs asked; gain = round(H(set distribution under pi) - sum over answers of P(answer) x H(set distribution under the posterior after that answer)); highest gain, ties to the earlier pair in (a, b) id order; entropy in nats
algorithm.sample_bests: for each sample, its best group (highest group score with that sample's weights, ties by id); computed once
algorithm.stop: stop when answers >= max_pairs, or answers >= min_pairs and round(stop probability) >= stop_prob (0.9 from 2026-11-17), where stop probability = sum of pi_s over the samples whose best group is among the current three (MMR on wbar, as recommend). (Changed 2026-11-17 from 'the most probable top-three set has probability >= stop_prob', which almost never holds with ~57 neighborhoods.) The next pair is still chosen by the expected entropy reduction of the top-three set
algorithm.groups: a one-apartment neighborhood counts under its parked host only when the host is within group_km and in the same state; otherwise it is its own group (groups lists the result)
algorithm.recommend: groups by MMR on wbar; in each, the three best buildings by round(score) desc, id; why = the two features with the largest wbar_k x (group centroid_k - mean over all buildings_k); gives_up: features in order of wbar_k x (centroid_k - mean of the other two picked centroids_k), negative ones only and never one of the two `why` features (centroids over the buildings shown); the first whose figure is unknown here (sq ft not published, parking not stated) is said plainly (gives_up_unknown true), or the first where this neighborhood's figure is worse than BOTH others' known figures by the margin in gives_up_margin (both figures as in the text: drive median minutes, lowest total, largest sq ft, median places, shortest park walk rounded) is compared; none: null. Figures are over the buildings shown
algorithm.what_would_change: multiply one weight by a nudge factor (more) or divide by it (less), renormalise, and see which group has the highest score; levels in `nudges` order, then features in order, then more before less; the first found where the first group changes (for the first neighborhood) or becomes this one (for the second and third)
algorithm.more_like_this: for each of the nine buildings shown, in order: up to 3 nearest other buildings by sqrt(sum_k wbar_k x (z_k - z'_k)^2), z = (features - feature_mean)/feature_sd, excluding the nine and the thumbnails already given; ties by id
algorithm.comparisons: values compared are rounded to round_decimals; ties go to the smaller id

conjoint.pool_rules:
Every task, in this order (the index is the tie-break):
two attributes: each pair of attributes (in ATTR_ORDER), every pair of different levels on each; A has the better
  level on the first attribute and the worse on the second (so neither apartment is better on everything);
three attributes: each triple, adjacent levels only (one step apart) on each; A better on the first; on the second
  and third, (A better, B better), (B, A) or (B, B) -- never A better on all three.
A task is [[attr, level of A, level of B], ...] with level indexes worst = 0.
conjoint.selection:
The next task index into the pool, or None after n_tasks. Candidates: the pool minus tasks already asked and
minus tasks on the same attributes as the previous one; the POOL_PREFILTER most utility-balanced at her mean
weights (round(|gap|), index); of those, the one with the largest expected reduction in posterior uncertainty:
the trace of the posterior covariance of the weights, expected over the three answers. Ties: lower index.
conjoint.levels_rule:
Attributes and levels, worst to best by feature value. Totals: the TOTAL_QUANTILES of the buildings' lowest
totals, rounded to $50 (the real spread); the other levels are the design's.
conjoint.priorities_rule:
Her weights in plain-word order (highest first; ties in FEATURES order) and the one-sentence summary. When the
spread of her weights (max - min) is below flat_below (flat_threshold of the samples), flat is true and the
sentence says nothing stood out, adding "if anything, X a little more" when the top weight leads by LEAN_STEP.
conjoint.nudge_rule:
Move one priority up or down one place: swap its weight with the weight of the priority just above (up) or just
below (down) it in priorities() order; nothing else changes (the sum stays 1). If the two weights are equal (to
ROUND decimals), the moved one is set NUDGE_TIE_STEP above (up) or below (down) the other, floored at 0, and the six
are renormalised to sum 1. At the top (up) or bottom (down) nothing changes. Returns the new weights.
conjoint.flat_rule: The FLAT_QUANTILE quantile of max - min over the weight samples: flatter than 99% of the prior's own vectors.

experiences.label: The Room-to-Breathe Experience
experiences.tagline: Towns farther out, with more space for you in Hamden and East Orange.

story.title: The Room-to-Breathe Experience
story.text: More room for you and your desk in Hamden and East Orange.

story.title: A weekday
story.text: In Hamden and East Orange the apartments have room for a proper desk. From the typical apartment a park is about 7 minutes on foot, and the supermarket is about 0.7 miles away.

story.title: Saturday night
story.text: From the typical apartment about 7 restaurants are within 1 mile, and bars are usually scarce. Having friends over is an easy evening.

story.title: Sunday with Mom and Dad
story.text: Seeing Mom and Dad is a long drive from most of these towns. Tolls run from about $15 to $44 round trip with a New York E-ZPass, and the train and bus take about 182 minutes.

story.title: What it costs
story.text: Rent is typically about $1,800 a month. The total with utilities and fees is typically about $2,020.

story.title: The catch
story.text: From most of these towns Mom and Dad are a long drive away. The typical apartment has only about 2 restaurants within a 10-minute walk.

experiences.about: This suits you if the apartment itself matters most, because you work from home. The typical apartment here is about 710 square feet, and in Hamden and East Orange there is room for a separate desk. In exchange you usually live farther from Mom and Dad, and what you can walk to depends on the town.

life_here.text: Soverel Park is a 14-minute walk for the daily loop. Monte Irvin Orange Park is a 48-acre Olmsted-designed county park with walking paths, athletic fields and a playground. Watsessing Dog Park is 1.5 miles away.
